o1.biggest_strength: Excellent mathematical breakdown of the 20% cut break-even point and the true cost of extending the credit window.
o1.biggest_mistake: It proposes a 40% year-one commission tier that adds $46,000 in unbudgeted commission costs on top of the allocated $40,000 perk budget.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the commission rate at 30% for all tiers and rely solely on the $40,000 perk budget to reward top partners without blowing out finance's constraints.

o2.biggest_strength: Brilliant financial acumen, specifically showing that even a 5-point commission raise would cost $74,550 to justify keeping one flat rate while using perks to reward top partners.
o2.biggest_mistake: Charging the free Podia plans against the $40k hard cash budget is a bit overly conservative since marginal software costs are near zero, but it's a safe accounting move.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: It is already a 10, but explicitly noting that the free plans don't cost hard cash could have freed up $12k for more partner grants.

reason: Both outputs are exceptional at crunching the lifetime value maths and shutting down the 20% cut. However, Output 2 rightly calculates that raising the commission rate would blow the budget and restricts rewards to the $40k perk allocation, whereas Output 1 blithely adds $46,000 in unapproved commission costs.
